# iFixPhones

> Phone, iPad and tablet repair shop in San Antonio, Texas, at 9055 Marbach Rd, Suite 105. Walk-ins welcome, open 7 days. Mobile repair is also available: a technician comes to the customer's home or work anywhere around San Antonio. Most screen repairs take about 10 minutes.

## Contact and hours

- Shop: 9055 Marbach Rd, Suite 105, San Antonio, TX
- Shop phone (calls and texts): (210) 773-3548
- Mobile repair line: (210) 724-2800
- Website: https://ifixphones.net
- Hours: Monday to Saturday 10 AM to 8 PM, Sunday 12 PM to 6 PM
- No appointment needed at the shop. Mobile repair is booked online or by calling (210) 724-2800.

## Repairs

- Screens: cracked, black or not responding. Most take about 10 minutes.
- Batteries: phone dies fast or shuts off. 15 to 20 minutes.
- Charging ports, back glass, cameras, speakers, microphones and buttons
- Water damage
- Soldering, unlocking and data recovery
- Brands: iPhone, Samsung Galaxy, Google Pixel, Motorola, OnePlus, iPad and Galaxy Tab

## Screen options

- Incell: the lowest-price option. No warranty, and not recommended for long-term use.
- OLED: the best aftermarket screen, with deep blacks and accurate color. 30-day warranty for glitches only. Offered for iPhone 13 Pro and newer Pro models, iPhone 17 and iPhone Air.
- Original: a refurbished original or a genuine Apple part, closest to factory.
- The shop tells each customer exactly which part goes in their phone.

## Prices and warranty

- Prices depend on the exact model and part, so the shop gives a free quote by text. Request one at https://ifixphones.net/#quote or text a photo to (210) 773-3548.
- Soft OLED screens have a 30-day warranty for glitches that happen on their own. It isn't breakage coverage: drops, pressure, bending or liquid aren't covered, even if the glass isn't cracked.
- Incell screens have no warranty.
- Every screen is tested with the customer before they pay.
- Mobile repair has a trip fee based on distance, quoted before the visit is booked.

## After a screen repair

- If a new screen turns on but doesn't respond to touch, a force restart often fixes it and doesn't erase anything.
- iPhone 8 and newer: press and quickly release volume up, then volume down, then press and hold the side button until the Apple logo appears.
- Samsung Galaxy: hold the side button and volume down together for 7 seconds or more.
- Steps with pictures: https://ifixphones.net/#after

## Other services

- Buys used phones for cash, cracked or working: https://ifixphones.net/#sell
- Repairs for schools and businesses, with pricing for groups of devices: https://ifixphones.net/#business
